# Stanford University
Founded in 1885 by Leland and Jane Stanford as a memorial to their son, Stanford University opened in 1891 on their former Palo Alto farm. Modeled after leading Eastern universities like Cornell, it emphasized inclusive, non-sectarian education from its early years. The campus combined English university architectural styles with California heritage and was designed by landscape architect Frederick Law Olmsted. Despite early financial challenges following Leland Stanford’s death and major damage from the 1906 earthquake, Stanford grew to include four professional graduate schools—Medicine, Law, Education, and Business—and established the SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory in 1962.
Under engineering professor Frederick Terman’s leadership in the 1940s and 1950s, Stanford embraced entrepreneurship, founding the Stanford Industrial Park and fostering the high-tech industry that became Silicon Valley. The university’s admissions became highly selective, with an acceptance rate of about 4%. Stanford enrolls approximately 7,000 undergraduates and over 10,000 graduate students, with a commitment to diversity and robust financial aid. It sits on an 8,180-acre campus that includes extensive research facilities like the SLAC accelerator and Jasper Ridge Biological Preserve.
Academically, Stanford comprises seven schools with graduate and undergraduate programs emphasizing research and interdisciplinary studies. Known for innovations in the natural sciences and technology, Stanford contributed foundational work to DNA synthesis, laser physics, Internet protocols, and entrepreneurial ventures such as Google and Cisco. The university’s student life features over 600 student organizations, diverse housing options, and numerous traditions, including the storied Stanford Axe rivalry with UC Berkeley. Its athletics program is among the most successful in the NCAA Division I, with notable achievements in many sports.
Governed by a 38-member board of trustees, Stanford’s endowment is one of the largest in academia at $36.5 billion (2023), supporting a broad spectrum of academic, research, and infrastructural initiatives. With a faculty including 58 Nobel laureates and numerous other distinguished scholars, Stanford is consistently ranked among the top universities globally and is recognized as a leader in innovation, education, and entrepreneurship.
